references.context: Commutative algebra: polynomial algebra R[X_i : i in I] over a commutative unital coefficient ring R, for an arbitrary set I of independent indeterminates; each polynomial has finite monomial support. Includes the one-variable and finite-variable cases and polynomial algebras over fields and quotient coefficient rings.
references.matching_note: Reviewed original source's polynomial expression with the common multivariate-polynomial construction. Index-set size and base coefficient ring specialize the same general commutative unital polynomial algebra; do not conflate it with localization, polynomial evaluation, the polynomial quotient or degree.

amendments.review_rationale: Read opposite category with identical object collection, all hom-set directions reversed, and reversed composition preserving the categorical identity and associativity laws.
amendments.reason: Reviewed the full original independent source meaning, all prior effective references and relevant mathematical contexts; retained source conventions, avoiding circular defining clauses and preserving reusable prerequisite identities.

references.disposition: The reversal of every morphism direction is the defining hom assignment of the opposite category. The hom-sets of the ambient category C are underlying category data; declaring this equality a separate prerequisite risks circularity.

Reversed composition g^{op}∘_{C^{op}}f^{op}=(f∘_C g)^{op} is the construction's defining composition rule, not an independently assumed concept. General categorical composition is part of the existing category structure.
The opposite category does not replace or dualize the objects themselves, only the morphisms and composition order.

references.context: Multilinear algebra: exterior power Λ^p_B M of a module M over commutative ring B, as alternating quotient of M^{⊗p}, with Λ^0_B M=B and the wedge product; instantiated here for the Kähler differential module.
references.reason: Exterior powers are reusable module constructions distinct from symmetric or ordinary tensor powers, and form the graded pieces of the de Rham complex.

references.reason: General graded cochain complexes are independently useful; the de Rham differential is a particular such construction and should not be its own prerequisite.

references.disposition: This Leibniz-compatible differential rule extends the universal derivation and is not a tensor product operation.

amendments.review_rationale: Read the Cohen ring as a complete discrete valuation ring whose unique maximal ideal equals the ideal generated by a prime integer, avoiding confusion with the Cohen–Macaulay condition.

references.context: Elementary number theory: positive prime integer p>1 whose only positive divisors are 1 and p, mapped to p·1_R under the canonical integer-to-unital-ring homomorphism ℤ→R.
references.reason: Primality of a positive integer is a reusable prerequisite, distinct from a prime ideal, prime element of an arbitrary ring or merely characteristic p.

references.context: Commutative algebra: principal ideal (p)=pR={pr:r∈R} generated by the image of a prime integer p in a commutative unital ring R; in the Cohen-ring formulation this equals the unique maximal ideal.
references.reason: A principal ideal generated by one ring element is independently definable; its equality with the maximal ideal is the Cohen-ring hypothesis.

references.disposition: The term denotes a complete discrete valuation ring of specified residue characteristic, not the depth/dimension Cohen–Macaulay property.
